rationale: PINS THE RESOLUTION RULE FOR A REDECLARED CLASS NAME, which is where `overrides` edges were being invented. `R6Class("AC", …)` is a constructor call evaluated top to bottom and `inherit = AC` inside it is an ordinary lookup at that point in the file, so the base in scope is the nearest PRECEDING DECLARATION of that name — not the union of every declaration of it, and not the last one in the file. The corpus shape that makes this unavoidable: R6's own test suite declares a class named `AC` NINETEEN times in one file (R6/tests/testthat/test-clone.R) with a different member set each time, and 6 of the 8 corpus files that carry an `overrides` edge redeclare a class name (measured by validation/m14/fixtures/r/probe-overrides-scoping.ts, population 2184 admitted files / 16 repositories / production parseFile / 0 parse failures). (1) LINE 20 vs LINE 21: two declarations of `AC`, the first with `first_only` and the second with `second_only`. `BC` at line 22 inherits the binding at line 21, so `BC` overrides `second_only` and NOT `first_only` — `overrides BC -> first_only` is forbidden because the base in scope does not declare that member. A union-keyed pass emits exactly that edge. (2) LINE 28 is the same base resolved across an intervening class declaration, so `DC` overrides `second_only` and not `first_only` too; under a `last`-declaration rule both derived classes still resolve to line 21 here, so this case alone cannot separate `preceding` from `last`. (3) LINE 37 inherits `Ghost`, a name this file never binds. `extends EC -> Ghost` IS emitted, because `extends` records the name written in the source and needs no declaration to exist; `overrides EC -> second_only` is forbidden, because asserting it would require inventing a base class with that member. The asymmetry is the point and it is deliberate. The decline is counted as `metadata.callAttribution.overridesBasesNotDeclaredEarlierInFile` = 1 here, so "no edges emitted" cannot be read as "this corpus contains no undeclared inheritance". (4) LINE 44 declares a class that shares BOTH member names with `BC` and inherits nothing: `overrides Standalone -> first_only` and `overrides Standalone -> second_only` are forbidden, and this is the harder half of the case than F12's three distinct names, because a name-keyed pass has no way to tell `Standalone` from `BC` at all. All four `overrides` edges sit at 0.95 and carry `overridingMember` and `overriddenClass`, because a bare `second_only` target names a member of four classes in this file. (5) LINES 65-67 are the case that separates `preceding` from `last`, and cases 1-4 cannot: in all four the derived class sits BELOW the last declaration of its base, so both rules name the same declaration and agree. Here `FC` at line 66 inherits the `AC` bound at line 65 `{alpha_only}`, and line 67 rebinds `AC` to `{omega_only}` out of scope at line 66. `preceding` emits `overrides FC -> alpha_only` and forbids `omega_only`; `last` resolves the base to line 67 and emits NOTHING; `union` sees `alpha_only` and agrees with `preceding`. So case 5 rejects `last` without rejecting `union`, cases 1-2 reject `union` without rejecting `last`, and the file needs both. That separation was added after `--mutants` reported `src-overrides-base-is-last-declaration` SURVIVED all 22 fixtures: the fixture was wrong, not the mutant unfalsifiable, and the survivor is what said so.
